name: Copying Data
description: We often have to copy large volumes of information. Such operation can take up many computer resources. Therefore, in this problem you are advised to come up with a way to copy some part of a number array into another one, quickly. More formally, you've got two arrays of integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n and b 1 , b 2 , ..., b n of length n . Also, you've got m queries of two types: Copy the subsegment of array a of length k , starting from position x , into array b , starting from position y , that is, execute b y + q = a x + q for all integer q (0 ≤ q < k ) . The given operation is correct — both subsegments do not touch unexistent elements. Determine the value in position x of array b , that is, find value b x . For each query of the second type print the result — the value of the corresponding element of array b .
input_specification: The first line contains two space-separated integers n and m (1 ≤ n , m ≤ 10 5 ) — the number of elements in the arrays and the number of queries, correspondingly. The second line contains an array of integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n (| a i | ≤ 10 9 ) . The third line contains an array of integers b 1 , b 2 , ..., b n (| b i | ≤ 10 9 ) . Next m lines contain the descriptions of the queries. The i -th line first contains integer t i — the type of the i -th query (1 ≤ t i ≤ 2) . If t i = 1 , then the i -th query means the copying operation. If t i = 2 , then the i -th query means taking the value in array b . If t i = 1 , then the query type is followed by three integers x i , y i , k i (1 ≤ x i , y i , k i ≤ n ) — the parameters of the copying query. If t i = 2 , then the query type is followed by integer x i (1 ≤ x i ≤ n ) — the position in array b . All numbers in the lines are separated with single spaces. It is guaranteed that all the queries are correct, that is, the copying borders fit into the borders of arrays a and b .
output_specification: For each second type query print the result on a single line.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 292E — Copying Data [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
